summary: Returns the value as a locale code, or throws.
description: Exactly two ASCII letters, in either case — `"en"`, `"UK"`. A region or a script subtag, as in `"en-US"`, is rejected: this is the short language code, not a full BCP 47 tag.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a locale code.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a locale code.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireValidLocale("en"); // => "en"
requireValidLocale("UK"); // => "UK"
requireValidLocale("en-US"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidLocale("eng"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
